POST /apps/api/v1/exchange.description: Redeem a short-lived authentication artifact issued by this gateway. Send the registered application Origin header. The artifact can be redeemed once and must belong to that application. A successful response sets the HttpOnly sid session cookie and the readable csrf cookie. Browser clients must include credentials on later gateway calls. Mutable session requests send the csrf cookie value in X-CSRF-Token. Production cookies share the Asodya domain and use Secure when reached through HTTPS. This operation returns no user data.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: Must identify the registered application that receives the session.

400.description: Missing, expired, reused, or wrong-application artifact; unregistered or mismatched Origin.

PATCH /user/sync/v1/log-in.description: Sign in through the gateway using email and password, or an authenticated provider access token supplied by the Auth flow. The response data is a short-lived opaque exchange artifact, not a session cookie or a user profile. Pass that artifact to the registered application exchange endpoint. The optional app identifies the initiating application and defaults to certifications. Email and IP limits apply, with progressive delay for repeated attempts. Invalid credentials return 401.

POST /user/sync/v1/sign-up.description: Create an account through the configured identity provider. Send email, password, optional display_name, and the initiating app. If the provider establishes a session immediately, data contains an exchange artifact. If email confirmation is required, the response is still 201 but data is null and the message explains the confirmation requirement. Use password sign-in after confirmation. Requests are limited by IP and email.

POST /user/sync/v1/oauth/start.description: Start backend-driven OAuth for the initiating application. Supported configured providers include Google, GitHub, and Microsoft/Azure. Microsoft is normalized to Azure. The response contains authorization_url for browser navigation. The gateway stores a short-lived state and PKCE verifier. Preserve the returned state and submit the provider code to the callback endpoint. This operation does not establish a browser session.

POST /user/sync/v1/oauth/callback.description: Complete the OAuth flow using the provider code and state from the start operation. A successful response contains a short-lived exchange artifact for the initiating application. Missing, expired, or already consumed state fails. Provider failures return 400. The callback preserves the existing provider response contract; real-provider compatibility must be distinguished from local contract tests.

POST /apps/support/v1/attachments.description: Upload one multipart file for a support message. A real authenticated user session is required, including for an administrator. Send the matching CSRF cookie/header. The maximum file size is 15 MiB. A successful response contains attachment_reference. Pass that reference in a ticket or message request. This operation does not create a ticket. Missing storage configuration returns 503; storage failure returns 502.

POST /apps/api/v1/client-error.description: Submit a frontend error report. Browser requests must come from an allowed Asodya or development origin. Anonymous clients can submit reports. The gateway limits intake to ten reports per minute per IP. It derives identity, session, client IP, user agent, and server time from the request context. Client-supplied values for these server fields do not establish identity. The 202 response means the report was queued for background storage.

GET /apps/api/v1/client-error.description: List recent frontend error reports. Administrator authorization is required. Use limit from 1 to 200 and non-negative skip for pagination. The response contains total for this result page and an errors array. Error records can contain operational details and user context, so this operation is not available to ordinary sessions.
